description: Figure 6(a) is a grouped vertical bar chart illustrating the distribution of datasets over time for the five most frequent researcher locations and all other locations combined. The horizontal axis represents the category "Year," ordered chronologically from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis represents the "Number of datasets" using a logarithmic scale (base 10), ranging from $10^0$ to $10^2$, with major tick labels and corresponding horizontal grid lines at $10^0$, $10^1$, and $10^2$. The chart features grouped bars for each year, where each individual bar within a group represents a specific researcher location as indicated by the legend. The locations and their corresponding colors are "Other" (blue), "USA" (orange), "IN" (green), "UK" (red), "IT" (purple), and "DE" (brown). Within each year's cluster, the bars are arranged side-by-side in the order they appear in the legend. In the earliest years shown (2012 to 2014), only the USA category is represented, featuring the shortest bars in the chart which rest exactly at the $10^0$ mark (indicating a value of 1). As the years progress, more locations appear, with all six categories represented from 2017 to 2022. The tallest bars in the chart belong to the "Other" category in the years 2020 and 2021, which peak just below the $10^2$ mark. The "USA" category also displays consistently taller bars relative to the remaining specific countries, peaking between $10^1$ and $10^2$ in 2020 and 2021. There are no specific bars visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines.
